name: Doxorubicin
route_note: IV injection/infusion; pegylated liposomal (Doxil/Caelyx) and liposomal (Myocet) forms also IV

discovery.note: Isolated from a mutant strain of Streptomyces peucetius (var. caesius) obtained by mutagenesis of the daunorubicin producer.

tagline: Red anthracycline antibiotic with broad anticancer activity and cumulative cardiotoxicity
summary: Doxorubicin is an anthracycline that intercalates into DNA and traps topoisomerase II, causing lethal double-strand breaks. It is one of the most broadly active cytotoxic drugs, used in breast cancer, lymphomas, leukaemias and sarcomas, with a lifetime dose limit because of dose-dependent cardiomyopathy.
mechanism: The planar anthraquinone ring inserts between DNA base pairs while the daunosamine sugar sits in the minor groove.
Doxorubicin stabilises the topoisomerase II–DNA cleavage complex, preventing re-ligation and leaving double-strand breaks that trigger apoptosis. It also evicts histones from chromatin.
Redox cycling of the quinone generates reactive oxygen species; combined with inhibition of topoisomerase IIβ in cardiomyocytes, this is linked to cumulative cardiotoxicity.
uses: Ovarian, bladder, thyroid and gastric cancer
Liposomal forms: ovarian cancer, Kaposi sarcoma, multiple myeloma

history.title: Daunorubicin
history.detail: Farmitalia and Rhône-Poulenc independently isolate daunorubicin, the parent anthracycline.

history.title: Doxorubicin reported
history.detail: Arcamone et al. describe adriamycin from a mutant Streptomyces strain.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Adriamycin.

history.title: ABVD
history.detail: Bonadonna introduces ABVD for Hodgkin lymphoma.

history.title: Cardiotoxicity defined
history.detail: Von Hoff and colleagues describe the steep rise in heart-failure risk above about 550 mg/m² cumulative dose.

history.title: Doxil
history.detail: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin approved for AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma, the first FDA-approved nanomedicine.

history.title: Doxil shortage
history.detail: A manufacturing failure at a contract supplier causes a prolonged US shortage of liposomal doxorubicin, leading FDA to permit temporary importation of Lipodox.

pk.metabolism: hepatic aldo-keto reductase to doxorubicinol (active); deglycosidation

safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning for cardiomyopathy, secondary malignancies, extravasation and tissue necrosis, and severe myelosuppression; reduce dose in hepatic impairment.

facts: Its red colour has earned it the nickname 'red devil' among patients.
Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (Doxil) was the first FDA-approved nanoparticle drug in 1995.
